deep.reconstruction:
Setting (implicit; inferred from this page, the previous page and DA §358). n is a prime with n ≡ 1 (mod 3) and f = (n-1)/3. The nonzero residues mod n split into three classes C0, C1, C2 according to ind x mod 3. The Gaussian periods p, p', p'' are the sums of ζ^x (ζ = e^{2πi/n}) over the three classes. R = (-1+√-3)/2. The resolvent is q = p + R p' + R² p''. In modern terms this is the cubic Gauss sum g(χ) for the cubic character χ(x) = R^{ind x}. Also q' = p + R² p' + R p'' = g(χ̄).

(1) Table of cyclotomic numbers of order 3. (ij) is the number of x in C_i with x+1 in C_j. Gauss records:
- (00) = a-1
- (01) = (10) = (22) = b
- (02) = (11) = (20) = c
- (12) = (21) = a

This is the standard reduction to essentially three unknowns. The usual modern (Dickson) notation is A, B, C, D with D = A+1; Gauss writes a := D. The second and third columns re-express the same nine numbers under relabelled index pairs. The third column is the transpose (ij) → (ji), consistent because the matrix is symmetric here. The second column looks like a relabelling of classes, e.g. a different generator or the action of x ↦ 1/x or x ↦ -1-x.

Row sums:
- (00)+(01)+(02)+1 = (10)+(11)+(12) = (20)+(21)+(22) = f = (n-1)/3. The '+1' accounts for x = -1, which lies in C0, since x+1 = 0.
- Hence a+b+c = (n-1)/3.

(2) The Jacobi-sum relation q² = (3a-1 + 3bR + 3cR²) q'. In modern form, g(χ)² = J(χ,χ) g(χ²) with J(χ,χ) = 3a-1+3bR+3cR². This follows by multiplying out p², pp', … with the cyclotomic numbers, as on the previous page: pp' = (10)p + (11)p' + (12)p'', etc. A crossed-out attempt 'qq' = …' is abandoned.

(3) q³ = ½ n (M + N√-27). The reasoning [my filling]:
- q q' = χ(-1) n = n, because χ(-1) = 1 for a cubic character.
- So q³ = J q q' = n J.
- Writing R = (-1+√-3)/2 gives J = (3a-1 - 3(b+c)/2) + (3(b-c)/2)√-3 = ½(M + N√-27), with M = 6a-2-3b-3c and N = b-c.

(4) Norm of J. n = J·J̄ = (3a-1+3bR+3cR²)(3a-1+3bR²+3cR) = (3a-1 - (3b+3c)/2)² + 27((b-c)/2)². Equivalently 4n = M² + 27N², which is the DA §358 representation.

(5) Solving back for a, b, c from M, N. From 6a+6b+6c = 2n-2 and M = 6a-2-3b-3c:
- M = 9a - n - 1, i.e. 9a - 1 = M + n and 9a = M + n + 1.
- 9b + 9c = 2n - 4 - M and 9b - 9c = 9N.
- So 18b = 2n - 4 - M + 9N and 18c = 2n - 4 - M - 9N.

(6) Congruence condition. Let g be a suitable cube root of unity mod n, i.e. g² + g + 1 ≡ 0. Then 3a - 1 + 3gb + 3g²c ≡ 0 (mod n). This is J(χ,χ) ≡ 0 modulo a prime of Z[R] above n, a Stickelberger-type congruence. Gauss then substitutes the expressions for a, b, c in M, N, n. Multiplying by 6 [my reconstruction] gives (2M - 4) + g(-M - 4 + 9N) + g²(-M - 4 - 9N) ≡ 0. Using 1 + g + g² ≡ 0, this reduces to 3M + 9N(g - g²) ≡ 0, i.e. M ≡ -3N(g - g²) (mod n). This congruence fixes the sign of N relative to the choice of g (g - g² ≡ ±√-3). Gauss's display ('2M-2' above the line, coefficients ±3N g, '≡ 6') is only partly legible and appears to be an intermediate or slipped form of this.

(7) Numerical check, n = 97:
- 4·97 = 388 = 19² + 27·1², so M = 19, N = 1.
- a = (19+97+1)/9 = 13.
- 2n - 4 - M = 171, so b = (171+9)/18 = 10 and c = (171-9)/18 = 9.
- a+b+c = 32 = 96/3, as required.
- The congruence holds with g = 61: 38 + 30·61 + 27·35 = 2813 = 29·97.

Purpose: determine the cyclotomic numbers of order 3 and the cube of the Lagrange resolvent. This feeds the explicit solution of the cubic period equation on the next page, which has the factor 1 - (M+3)n, i.e. x³ + x² - f x - ((M+3)n - 1)/27 = 0.
errors: Relation 9a - 1 = M + n is correct, since M = 9a - n - 1. The machine transcription's doubt is unwarranted.

In the final congruence block, multiplying 3a-1+3gb+3g²c by 6 gives constant term 2M+2n-4 ≡ 2M-4 (not 2M-2) and N-coefficients ±9N (not ±3N). Gauss's '2M-2', '3N' and '≡ 6' are either a slip or an incomplete intermediate form. The correct consequence is M + 3N(g - g²) ≡ 0 (mod n).
The congruence 3a-1+3gb+3g²c ≡ 0 holds only for the appropriate one of the two cube roots of unity mod n. For n = 97 it holds with g = 61 but not with g = 35. Gauss leaves this choice implicit.
Next page writes cube root of ¼n(M+N√-27) = θ√n. With this page's q³ = ½n(M+N√-27), the modulus requires ½, not ¼. This may be a different normalisation or a slip on that page.
The struck line 'qq' = 3a-1+3cR+3bR'' was abandoned. It is not used.

results.what: Cyclotomic numbers of order 3 reduce to (00)=a-1, (01)=(10)=(22)=b, (02)=(11)=(20)=c, (12)=(21)=a, with a+b+c=(n-1)/3
results.modern_name: Cyclotomic numbers of order 3 (Dickson's A,B,C,D with D=A+1)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, Disquisitiones Arithmeticae §358 (1801); systematised by Dickson (1935)

results.what: q² = (3a-1+3bR+3cR²) q', i.e. square of resolvent = Jacobi sum × conjugate resolvent
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (implicit in DA §358); Jacobi (1827/1837) in general form

results.what: q³ = ½ n (M + N√-27) with 4n = M² + 27N², M = 6a-2-3b-3c, N = b-c
results.modern_name: Cube of the cubic Gauss sum: g(χ)³ = pJ(χ,χ); representation 4p = L² + 27M²
Cyclotomic numbers of order 3 expressed via the representation 4p = L²+27M² (Dickson's formulas)

results.what: Congruence 3a-1+3gb+3g²c ≡ 0 (mod n) for a cube root of unity g mod n, giving M ≡ -3N(g-g²), which fixes the sign of N
results.modern_name: Jacobi sum ≡ 0 modulo a prime above p (Stickelberger-type congruence) / normalisation of the cubic Jacobi sum
results.usually_credited_to: Jacobi (1827, cubic residues), Kummer; Stickelberger (1890) in general

deep.surprise_reason: The main content is the order-3 cyclotomic numbers and 4n = M²+27N², which is published Gauss (DA §358). The extra congruence fixing the sign of N via a cube root of unity mod n is a Jacobi/Stickelberger-type refinement. Gauss's Nachlass on cubic residues is known to contain related material, so this is a notable but not unexpected unpublished detail.

transcription_corrections: Line '9a-1 [?] = M+n' should read 9a - 1 = M + n (or with ≡). It is correct as written.
In the struck line 'qq' = 3a-1+3cR+3bR'', the last term is 3bR² (R' is a misreading).
'9b-9c = 9N': the image shows a corrected operator; the intended relation is 9b - 9c = 9N, since N = b - c.
Right-hand numbers '171' and '19·1' are 2n-4-M = 171 and M=19, N=1 (or 9N = 9·1). They are auxiliary numbers for computing b and c.
In the second column, '[-12-] 22' (row 10) and '[-1-]12' (row 21) are overwritten entries. The final values are 22 and 12.
